thread:
maria: FYI production TP job 8-node suddenly started hitting 30s+ step timeouts on a couple of customers. Not a full hang but heavy tail and then the orchestrator kills the job.
jon: Which cluster/commit? any recent runtime changes?
maria: us-west-2, dedicated. Runtime build b2026 deployed ~1h before the spikes (deploy-bot: release b2026 to us-west-2).
aline: I pulled a flamegraph from the perf traces for a slow step. High-level: all-reduce cost jumped and kernel selector oscillating between two kernels each step.
sam: Oscillating selector? did autotuner change or new kernel heuristics land in b2026? I pushed a tuning tweak yesterday that biases kernel A for seq<=1024, kernel B otherwise.
linh: We also changed the batching heuristic to be more aggressive for short sequences — might interact with the kvcache eviction pattern.
kevin: Can you paste the small profile snippet? even a diff would help.\maline: here's the truncated perf output I collected (nvprof-like):
```
# step 421 slow
kernel_select: chosen=kernelA  (lat 0.8ms)  prev=kernelB
allreduce:  12.1ms (was 1.9ms baseline)
kvcache: eviction spikes coincident with step start (lots of memcopy)
cpu->gpu memcpy: 3.3ms
overlap compute/comm: 10% effective
```
jon: Allreduce 12ms from normal ~2ms is huge. Does nccl log show fallback to ring vs tree?
aline: NCCL logs show switch to different algorithm sometimes, and retransmits on ranks 3/6 in the slow steps. Looks like small oscillations cause shape changes that flip kernel choice and NCCL algorithm.
sam: That flipping could be from micro-batching differences: if the batch packing crosses a threshold we pick a different kernel and different allreduce plan.
maria: Also seeing k-v cache evictions at the start of the step which increases memcpy and changes buffer alignment. I suspect alignment + kernel selector boundary = different collective size profile.
kevin: Can we reproduce locally with --simulate-batching to force the same microbatch sizes? If so we can instrument kernel selector decisions per-step.
linh: I reproduced with a repro harness on 4 nodes (reduced) by toggling kvcache capacity. When kvcache hits 75% full it does a compaction which moves segments and changes tensor strides leading to different kernel path.
jon: So compaction -> memcopies -> changed buffer alignments -> kernel selector flips -> different reduction algorithm -> allreduce slowdown. Nice.
sam: What about comm/compute overlap? Even if allreduce slower, we should overlap. Why overlap collapsed to 10%?
aline: Overlap collapsed because memcopy happened right before collective start, starving the GPUDirect path; plus our async allreduce enqueue point assumes KV cache stable. If compaction moves data after enqueue, we serialize.
kevin: Two short-term mitigations: 1) disable aggressive kvcache compaction for now, 2) add hysteresis to kernel selector to avoid flipping kernel for tiny alignment differences.
maria: I'll roll a quick patch to reduce compaction frequency and revert the selector bias. Can we try a canary in the dedicated cluster?
jon: Deploy-bot: please announce canary window.
deploy-bot: scheduling canary deploy b2026-hotfix1 to us-west-2-dedicated in 10m.
sam: Also we should add an assertion in selector telemetry to log reason codes (alignment, seq_len, dtype) so we can correlate in SLO hits.
kevin: Agree. Also add NCCL alg tags to traces so we can filter steps where algorithm switched.
aline: For the postmortem we should include: repro steps (kvcache cap, microbatch pattern), perf graphs (allreduce latency distribution), kernel selector trace, and the hotfix diff.
maria: Action items: (1) maria -> deploy hotfix to reduce compaction and revert selector bias (in 30m), (2) sam -> add selector hysteresis PR, (3) aline -> add NCCL alg tagging to profiler, (4) kevin -> run 8-node repro overnight and collect traces.
jon: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread and paste canary metrics once available. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: alert suppressed for policy "tp-step-timeout" until b2026-hotfix1 deployment
maria: Canary showed 10% tail latency drop after hotfix on initial run, need longer run but promising.
kevin: Overnight run looks stable so far (8h, no timeouts). I'll upload traces to the shared perf bucket.
aline: Nice work. We'll schedule a short retro tomorrow to capture learnings and get a durable fix for the kvcache/kernel interaction.
maria: Closing for now, will reopen if we see regressions.
